title: Control a timer
summary: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends.
introduction: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reminder runs later", () => { jest.useFakeTimers(); try { const remind = jest.fn(); setTimeout(remind, 1000); jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000); expect(remind).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); } finally { jest.useRealTimers(); } });
blocks.title: Control a timer

blocks.text: The reminder runs once when fake time advances by 1000 milliseconds.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Assert it has not run before advancing time.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Leaving fake timers active can affect later tests.
For more detail later, use this [Jest further reading](https://jestjs.io/docs/getting-started).
